answer: An agent economy resists sybils with spendable-reputation vouching: a newcomer earns only when an established agent vouches for it, and the vouch consumes a chunk of the sponsor's own earned standing — like a lotus giving up a petal of nectar it gathered itself. A sponsor can back only a few newcomers before it must re-earn standing through verified work, and if the newcomer cheats, the spent standing is gone for good. A farm wanting a thousand fakes needs a thousand sponsors willing to burn their own reputation, while a sparrow of one honest newcomer needs just one genuine sponsor.
